title: The same contractor, more than one contract paid past its ceiling or its end date
question: Do contracts paid above their ceiling or long after their end date cluster on particular contractors?
finding: Of 24,716 paid contracts with a ceiling, 148 (0.60%) were paid above it or two fiscal years past their end date. Among 1,222 contractors with five or more such contracts, 10 have two or more of the 148. 3 of them have more than their mix of work and departments would give at the one-in-a-hundred level; with 1,222 contractors tested, about 12 would cross that line by chance. At the top: Core & Main LP (3 of 11 contracts, 0.27 expected); San Francisco Women Against Rape (3 of 19 contracts, 0.34 expected); Towne Ford Sales (2 of 5 contracts, 0.12 expected). That is no more than chance would produce. 8 of the 10 repeat cases are suppliers of goods, where a ceiling is a limit on orders.
how: The two contract-table tests (paid above the ceiling after the data causes are removed; paid two or more fiscal years after the end date on record) are counted for every contractor with five or more paid contracts, leaving out rents and public bodies. The expected number is the sum, over the contractor's contracts, of the rate of such events among all contracts of the same kind of work in the same department. "Chance" is the probability of at least that many events at that expected number; contractors with two or more are listed, the least likely first.
limits: Both tests measure what the table failed to record as much as what happened: a ceiling keyed late, an end date not updated, tax and freight on goods. Neither test sees a contract that was amended on the record; so this is not a measure of overruns, only of payments the table cannot account for.
